entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

# The CANON repo's own CI — Claudinite's test suite + its own conformance sweep
# on every PR. Not consumer wiring (consumers ship no workflow, #385).
name: CI
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  # Dispatchable so a GITHUB_TOKEN-authored PR (whose push/open GitHub never
  # turns into a pull_request run — the recursion guard) can still get this
  # suite started on its branch: baselining's deliver() and any bot-authored
  # PR flow (#432, #565) dispatch it explicitly.
  workflow_dispatch:
defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash
jobs:
  test-and-conformance:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # Check out the PR's real head, not the synthetic refs/pull/N/merge commit
          # actions/checkout uses by default — otherwise HEAD is an ephemeral merge of
          # the branch into main, which the work-scoped squash-merge-history check would
          # (correctly, for that synthetic commit) flag. This makes CI evaluate exactly
          # what the local Stop hook does: the branch tip. Falls back to github.sha on push.
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - name: Unit tests
        # THE test roots — a closed set of FOLDERS, each swept to any depth. Depth is
        # deliberately not enumerated: the previous form spelled out one glob per level of
        # nesting, so a test at an unlisted depth was silently never run — which is exactly
        # how vendoring/'s two files sat outside CI. `**` removes depth from the question;
        # what remains is the root list, and engine-tests/ci-test-roots.test.mjs fails the
        # moment a tracked test lands outside it. Adding a root is a deliberate CI edit;
        # adding a test is not.
        #   engine-tests/            engine/ (migrations included) + the other top-level canon code;
        #                            mirrors engine/'s inner structure, and stays canon-side
        #                            because engine/ ships to consumers exactly as-is (#385)
        #   packs/                   every canon pack's tests, each inside the pack it covers
        #   vendoring/               co-located with the vendor computer/writer they cover,
        #                            the fixture-consumer rehearsal included
        #   dev/tools/               maintainer-side tooling nothing at session time runs
        #   .claudinite/local/packs/ this repo's own local packs — tests live inside the tree
        # nullglob: a root with no tests drops out instead of reaching node as a literal pattern.
        run: |
          shopt -s globstar nullglob
          tests=(engine-tests/**/*.test.mjs packs/**/*.test.mjs vendoring/**/*.test.mjs dev/tools/**/*.test.mjs .claudinite/local/packs/**/*.test.mjs)
          # Deliberately oversubscribed. node --test defaults to one worker per core
          # minus one, which fits a CPU-bound suite; this one spends most of its wall
          # clock waiting — on git plumbing, spawned workers and converge fixtures — so
          # the cores idle at that default (measured on this tree: 106s wall against
          # 187s of user+sys on 4 cores). Doubling the workers: 106s -> 70s, with 16
          # buying only another 2s.
          #
          # TAP goes to a FILE, not the log. 2,448 tests emit ~13,000 lines at 5.3
          # lines each, and a failing run's one `not ok` sits wherever its file

content.content:
# lines each, and a failing run's one `not ok` sits wherever its file
          # finished — while GitHub's job-log API serves only a TAIL and the signed
          # blob URL that would serve the whole thing is proxy-blocked. So a red run
          # said `# fail 1` and nothing more, and five green local re-runs could not
          # name the test (#1170). Printing the failing blocks puts the identity in
          # the tail, where it can actually be read.
          status=0
          node --test --test-concurrency=$(( $(nproc) * 2 )) "${tests[@]}" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/tests.tap" || status=$?
          if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
            echo '::group::failing tests'
            grep -n -A 25 '^not ok' "$RUNNER_TEMP/tests.tap" || echo 'no `not ok` line — the runner died before reporting one'
            echo '::endgroup::'
          fi
          tail -n 12 "$RUNNER_TEMP/tests.tap"
          exit "$status"
      - name: Conformance sweep (world scope)
        # The tree as it stands — the pattern bootstrap wires into consumers.
        run: node engine/checks/check_the_world.mjs
      - name: Conformance sweep (work scope)
        # The CHANGE, not the tree: this branch's diff against the base branch, the
        # only scope that can see what a commit did rather than what the repo now
        # holds. It used to run at the session's Stop hook and nowhere else, so a
        # rule about the change was enforced only where a session happened to be.
        #
        # The recipe — fetch the base, skip the engine's own branches, refuse an
        # empty scope, sweep — lives in the engine entry point, which every member
        # vendors and runs by the same one line. This repo is the one that runs it
        # from the repo root instead of the mount.
        #
        # --branch explicitly: the checkout above is a detached head at the PR's real
        # head sha, where `rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` says "HEAD" and no branch name
        # is discoverable — so the skip for engine-authored branches would never fire.
        run: node engine/checks/ci-work-scope.mjs --branch "${{ github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}"
      - name: Growth write-surface gate
        # The lifecycle's capture runs (extract, dedup) are bounded to the repo's own
        # local packs. Unlike promote below, a capture run marks ITSELF — the pinned
        # commit subject its task doc gives it — so the gate self-gates and this step
        # runs on every PR, exiting 0 in ~no time on any other branch.
        run: node .claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/growth-scope-gate.mjs
      - name: Promote write-surface gate
        # The growth promote stage is the one change bounded to this canon's corpus roots — an
        # ordinary engine PR legitimately edits checks/ and engine/, so this cannot run on every
        # PR. It keys on the promote branch prefix (the task doc pins it) and fails the promote PR
        # if a changed path strays.
        if: contains(github.head_ref, 'growth-promote')
        run: node .claudinite/local/packs/claudinite/promote-scope-gate.mjs

entries.name: mcp__github__actions_get
entries.description:
Get details about specific GitHub Actions resources.
Use this tool to get details about individual workflows, workflow runs, jobs, and artifacts by their unique IDs.

resource_id.description:
The unique identifier of the resource. This will vary based on the "method" provided, so ensure you provide the correct ID:
- Provide a workflow ID or workflow file name (e.g. ci.yaml) for 'get_workflow' method.
- Provide a workflow run ID for 'get_workflow_run', 'get_workflow_run_usage', and 'get_workflow_run_logs_url' methods.
- Provide an artifact ID for 'download_workflow_run_artifact' method.
- Provide a job ID for 'get_workflow_job' method.

entries.name: mcp__github__get_job_logs
entries.description:
Get logs for GitHub Actions workflow jobs.
Use this tool to retrieve logs for a specific job or all failed jobs in a workflow run.
For single job logs, provide job_id. For all failed jobs in a run, provide run_id with failed_only=true.

failed_only.description: When true, gets logs for all failed jobs in the workflow run specified by run_id. Requires run_id to be provided.

job_id.description: The unique identifier of the workflow job. Required when getting logs for a single job.

return_content.description: Returns actual log content instead of URLs

run_id.description: The unique identifier of the workflow run. Required when failed_only is true to get logs for all failed jobs in the run.

tail_lines.description: Number of lines to return from the end of the log

Two always-testable rules the shelf's prose carried but no check did.

`web-speech` / `tts-voices-cached-empty` — a module-scope
`speechSynthesis.getVoices()` cache is empty for the page's life, so every
utterance falls back to the OS default voice with nothing thrown. Silent by
construction, which is what the pack's other call-site contracts are for.
A file that refreshes from `voiceschanged` is spared.

`macos` / `notarize-then-staple` — a release lane that submits to the notary
service and staples nowhere ships an artifact Gatekeeper can only open while
Apple is reachable. It passes on the submitting machine, whose ticket is
cached, so the failure only ever lands on a user's Mac.

Both prose paragraphs stay: each carries more than its check does — the
lazy-memo half of the voice rule, and `--wait` / `stapler validate` / which
container to staple in the notarization one.

Eight corpus claims about the environment no longer held when re-probed in a live
session. The largest is that the sandbox's egress proxy now authenticates
api.github.com as the session's own GitHub identity: a repo inside the session's
scope answers 200 with no Authorization header, and only a repo outside it 403s
("Use add_repo to request access"). Six places stated the blanket 403, or "no REST
credential", or "carries no repo token".

- searching-for-a-tool: select: resolves a short name now, so the rule no longer
  splits the two spellings. Its references entry named exactly this retirement
  condition.
- basics "Calling Edit": the read requirement binds only OUTSIDE the working
  directory and the session scratchpad, and a shell write does not satisfy it
  there - only a Read or the Write tool does. The rule's trigger changes with it,
  which is the deliberate rules-append-only advisory on this diff.
- git-github-advanced: the 403 claim rescoped; list_workflow_jobs and
  download_workflow_run_artifact readdressed as methods of actions_list and
  actions_get, which is where the GitHub MCP server now carries them.
- unattended-agents: the rule holds, but not by the symptom it named. GITHUB_TOKEN
  is set-but-empty and node's global fetch goes direct, so the failure arrives as
  GitHub's IP-keyed rate-limit 403, never a 401.
- The four task docs claiming no cross-repo git: git ls-remote reaches a repo
  outside the session's GitHub scope, so that boundary is the granted scope, not a
  missing capability, and the prose now says so.

Every verdict, corrected or not, is in the PR body with the probe behind it.

Refs #2054

* A task can decline while one of its own pull requests is open

`no-open-pr-of-this-task` recognises a round by the branch family the executor
mints it on, so a task whose pull requests carry neither a stable title nor a
fixed path — the two its sibling pending-round terms rest on — can still refuse
to stack a second round on an unreviewed one. It is the complement of
`fresh_pr`, which leaves an earlier round open.

The prefix moves to contract/task-branch.mjs, since the gate asks the question
before the executor has minted anything and neither side may spell it twice, and
the open-PR signal carries the head ref the listing already returned.

Refs #2042

* Four canon tasks change what they do to their pull requests

ci-performance opens a fresh pull request and does not run at all while one of
its own is still open: a performance fix is argued from an A/B that run measured,
so a second round cannot be folded into the first one's review.

growth-discover-packs opens a fresh one too — each run authors a different pack
for a different gap, so folding two into one review puts two unrelated packs in
front of the owner.

pack-version-history and claudinite-lifecycle/update supersede theirs. Both
recompute the whole answer from the base, so the round under review holds
nothing the next one does not, and a green round nobody merged is landed rather
than closed.

Refs #2042

* upstream-watch becomes revalidate-from-source, and supersedes

The task is named for what it does to the shelf — revalidate each pack against
the sources it declared — rather than for watching something upstream. A month
whose pull request nobody reviewed is retired by the next month's, which
recomputes the same answer from the sources and the anchors on the base.

Every live reference follows the name; the VERSIONS rows and the dashboard mock
keep the old one, being records of what happened.

Refs #2042

* ci-performance waits on its own parked run, not on its open PR

The gate is the previous run's state, not the artifact it left: `last-run-not-parked`
holds a task back while its newest run stands at any of the four parks, where
`last-run-not-failed` reads only the failure one. An unmerged pull request parks
on approval, which is not a fault, so the narrower term would let the task stack
a second round behind an unanswered one.

It reads the park kind the runs bundle already carries, so the branch-family
recognition goes: no signal field, no taskId through the evaluator, no shared
prefix module.

`holdsOnFailure` answers true for either term, a task holding behind every park
holding behind that one too, and the dashboard takes `holdsOnAnyPark` beside it —
without it a lane parked on approval renders its next calendar anchor while the
task declines every week.

Refs #2042

Two always-testable rules the shelf's prose carried but no check did.

`web-speech` / `tts-voices-cached-empty` — a module-scope
`speechSynthesis.getVoices()` cache is empty for the page's life, so every
utterance falls back to the OS default voice with nothing thrown. Silent by
construction, which is what the pack's other call-site contracts are for.
A file that refreshes from `voiceschanged` is spared.

`macos` / `notarize-then-staple` — a release lane that submits to the notary
service and staples nowhere ships an artifact Gatekeeper can only open while
Apple is reachable. It passes on the submitting machine, whose ticket is
cached, so the failure only ever lands on a user's Mac.

Both prose paragraphs stay: each carries more than its check does — the
lazy-memo half of the voice rule, and `--wait` / `stapler validate` / which
container to staple in the notarization one.

Eight corpus claims about the environment no longer held when re-probed in a live
session. The largest is that the sandbox's egress proxy now authenticates
api.github.com as the session's own GitHub identity: a repo inside the session's
scope answers 200 with no Authorization header, and only a repo outside it 403s
("Use add_repo to request access"). Six places stated the blanket 403, or "no REST
credential", or "carries no repo token".

- searching-for-a-tool: select: resolves a short name now, so the rule no longer
  splits the two spellings. Its references entry named exactly this retirement
  condition.
- basics "Calling Edit": the read requirement binds only OUTSIDE the working
  directory and the session scratchpad, and a shell write does not satisfy it
  there - only a Read or the Write tool does. The rule's trigger changes with it,
  which is the deliberate rules-append-only advisory on this diff.
- git-github-advanced: the 403 claim rescoped; list_workflow_jobs and
  download_workflow_run_artifact readdressed as methods of actions_list and
  actions_get, which is where the GitHub MCP server now carries them.
- unattended-agents: the rule holds, but not by the symptom it named. GITHUB_TOKEN
  is set-but-empty and node's global fetch goes direct, so the failure arrives as
  GitHub's IP-keyed rate-limit 403, never a 401.
- The four task docs claiming no cross-repo git: git ls-remote reaches a repo
  outside the session's GitHub scope, so that boundary is the granted scope, not a
  missing capability, and the prose now says so.

Every verdict, corrected or not, is in the PR body with the probe behind it.

nothing the next one does not, and a green round nobody merged is landed rather
than closed.

Refs #2042

* upstream-watch becomes revalidate-from-source, and supersedes

The task is named for what it does to the shelf — revalidate each pack against
the sources it declared — rather than for watching something upstream. A month
whose pull request nobody reviewed is retired by the next month's, which
recomputes the same answer from the sources and the anchors on the base.

Every live reference follows the name; the VERSIONS rows and the dashboard mock
keep the old one, being records of what happened.

Refs #2042

* ci-performance waits on its own parked run, not on its open PR

The gate is the previous run's state, not the artifact it left: `last-run-not-parked`
holds a task back while its newest run stands at any of the four parks, where
`last-run-not-failed` reads only the failure one. An unmerged pull request parks
on approval, which is not a fault, so the narrower term would let the task stack
a second round behind an unanswered one.

It reads the park kind the runs bundle already carries, so the branch-family
recognition goes: no signal field, no taskId through the evaluator, no shared
prefix module.

`holdsOnFailure` answers true for either term, a task holding behind every park
holding behind that one too, and the dashboard takes `holdsOnAnyPark` beside it —
without it a lane parked on approval renders its next calendar anchor while the
task declines every week.

Refs #2042

entries.description:
Tools for listing GitHub Actions resources.
Use this tool to list workflows in a repository, or list workflow runs, jobs, and artifacts for a specific workflow or workflow run.

perPage.description: Results per page for pagination (default: 30, max: 100)

resource_id.description:
The unique identifier of the resource. This will vary based on the "method" provided, so ensure you provide the correct ID:
- Do not provide any resource ID for 'list_workflows' method.
- Provide a workflow ID or workflow file name (e.g. ci.yaml) for 'list_workflow_runs' method, or omit to list all workflow runs in the repository.
- Provide a workflow run ID for 'list_workflow_jobs' and 'list_workflow_run_artifacts' methods.

filter.description: Filters jobs by their completed_at timestamp

workflow_jobs_filter.description: Filters for workflow jobs. **ONLY** used when method is 'list_workflow_jobs'

actor.description: Filter to a specific GitHub user's workflow runs.

branch.description: Filter workflow runs to a specific Git branch. Use the name of the branch.

event.description: Filter workflow runs to a specific event type

status.description: Filter workflow runs to only runs with a specific status

workflow_runs_filter.description: Filters for workflow runs. **ONLY** used when method is 'list_workflow_runs'

Both are declared checks — patterns over files, the ladder's highest check rung — and both ship `since: 2026-09-15`, so they bite at their real severity once the two-week window closes.

## What converted

| Prose | Became | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| `web-speech` — *"Voice lists load lazily — an empty `getVoices()` means 'not ready yet', not 'no voices'"* | `tts-voices-cached-empty` | blocking |
| `macos` — *"Notarize the distributed container, then staple it"* | `notarize-then-staple` | blocking |

**`tts-voices-cached-empty`** flags a module-scope `const/let/var … = speechSynthesis.getVoices()`. That call answers empty until the browser has loaded voices, so the cache stays empty for the page's life and every utterance falls back to the OS default voice — nothing throws, nothing logs, which is exactly what the pack's other call-site contracts exist to catch. A file that refreshes from a `voiceschanged` listener is spared, comments are stripped first, and test scaffolding and built bundles are out of scope.

**`notarize-then-staple`** flags a script or workflow that runs `notarytool submit` where nothing in the repo runs `stapler staple`. An unstapled artifact carries no ticket of its own, so Gatekeeper has to reach Apple the first time a user opens it — and never has to on the machine that submitted it, which is why the failure only ever appears on somebody else's Mac. Scoped to scripts, workflows and source: markdown neither flags nor excuses, so a runbook naming the command cannot silence the check.

## Proof

Each check has a fixture suite with a violating case and a false-positive guard per escape. Every guard was proved by mutating the declaration and watching that case bite, then restoring:

- removing `unlessFileMatches` → the `voiceschanged` case fires; removing `scanIgnoringComments` → a block-commented example fires; removing the test/vendor exclusions → the fake and the bundle fire.
- removing the comment anchor from `flagFilesMatching` → a commented-out `notarytool submit` fires; neutering `unlessSomeFileMatches` → both staple-present cases fire; widening `scanFiles` to markdown → the runbook case fires.

Both checks were also run over this repository's real tree and report nothing.

## The deletion test

Both paragraphs stay whole, each carrying something its check does not:

- the voice rule also covers a lazy memo *inside* a function (`cached ??= getVoices()`), which the module-scope signature cannot see;
- the notarization rule also carries `--wait`, `stapler validate`, and *which* container to staple.

## Notes

- Neither pack is declared here, so neither check runs in the canon; `check_the_world` and `check_the_work` are both clean, and the sweep gained no new advisory.
- The full suite is green apart from the six `packs/claude-code-web-users-support/test/session-start.test.mjs` cases that read the ambient `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED` and are red in every unattended session — #2031, already open, unrelated to this diff. They pass with the variable unset.
- Pack versions and `VERSIONS.md` rows are deliberately untouched: both are derived on the base branch after this lands.

input.commit_title: Canon prose to checks: a stale voice cache and an unstapled notarization (#2059)
input.commit_message:
Two always-testable rules the shelf's prose carried but no check did.

`web-speech` / `tts-voices-cached-empty` — a module-scope
`speechSynthesis.getVoices()` cache is empty for the page's life, so every
utterance falls back to the OS default voice with nothing thrown. A file that
refreshes from `voiceschanged` is spared.

`macos` / `notarize-then-staple` — a release lane that submits to the notary
service and staples nowhere ships an artifact Gatekeeper can only open while
Apple is reachable. It passes on the submitting machine, whose ticket is
cached, so the failure only ever lands on a user's Mac.

Both prose paragraphs stay: each carries more than its check does — the
lazy-memo half of the voice rule, and `--wait` / `stapler validate` / which
container to staple in the notarization one.

Claudinite-Automerge-Policy: under:packs

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/user/Claudinite/.claude/skills/merge-to-main

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`); when the change has an issue,
   the body carries `Closes #<issue>` on its own line.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --pr <pr>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --pr <pr>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it
   again. (1)
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read an issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.
